sources.title: Republic of Palau Second National Communication to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
sources.temporal_coverage: Palau climate vulnerability assessments and historic conditions reported in 2013; includes projections to 2050 and 2100.
sources.methodology: Melekeok climate assessment in a government UNFCCC communication, using field surveys and GIS.
sources.limitations: Dated site study; proposed actions are not completed adaptation.

sources.title: Palau Water Policy 2025–2045
sources.temporal_coverage: Water-sector conditions and policy priorities in the 2025–2045 policy; includes historical 2016 drought and cited climate projections.
sources.methodology: Government water policy synthesizing watershed and utility information.
sources.limitations: Some climate projections date to the 2015 policy.

sources.title: Disaster Risk and Climate Change Impact Survey in the Republic of Palau, Phase I
sources.organization: Palau Bureau of Cultural and Historical Preservation and University of Oregon researchers; supported by UNDP through the EDCR project
sources.temporal_coverage: Field survey conducted November 2019 and March 2020; includes flooding observed at Kayangel in April 2021.
sources.methodology: Targeted ten-site cultural survey using field observations and standardized condition forms.
sources.limitations: Selected heritage sites are not representative of Palau communities.

sources.title: Palau’s Rock Islands Southern Lagoon launches resilience strategy
sources.temporal_coverage: Resilience strategy launched in 2023; coastal fisheries management plan adopted in 2021.
sources.methodology: UNESCO publisher report on the locally developed Rock Islands Southern Lagoon resilience strategy.
sources.limitations: Short programme account; reports strategy activities and institutional arrangements, not independent impact estimates.

sources.title: Palau: Office of Climate Change — climate impacts and the Palau Climate Change Policy 2025
sources.organization: Office of Climate Change, Republic of Palau
sources.temporal_coverage: Official page summarizing the 2025 climate policy and climate projections through 2040 and later.
sources.methodology: Official climate-office page summarizing policy pillars and selected climate impacts and projections.
sources.limitations: Underlying projection methods and emissions scenario are not provided on the page; policy pillars are commitments, not delivered results.

sources.title: Enhancing disaster and climate resilience in Palau
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, Pacific Office
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports damage from Typhoon Haiyan in 2013 and El Niño drought in 2016; describes disaster-capacity activities in February 2020.
sources.methodology: UNDP report on disaster impacts, preparedness partnership and planned post-disaster assessment training.
sources.limitations: Historical programme account; training was scheduled, and reported losses are not a climate-attribution or conflict assessment.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 43–44 (printed pp. 44–45), Melekeok vulnerability assessment.
claims.paraphrase: The assessment placed most coastal homes, tourist lodging and utility lines within 30 metres of Melekeok’s high-water mark, vulnerable to sea rise, waves and typhoons.
claims.scenario: The 2013 assessment considers sea-level rise, storm surge and waves through 2100.
claims.limitations: 2013 estimate for the mapped coastal strip.

claims.locator: PDF p. 44 (printed p. 45), Melekeok coastal wastewater-treatment plant assessment.
claims.paraphrase: It identified the southern-coast wastewater plant as a low-lying mangrove-edge asset at risk of inundation, damage and sewage release.
claims.scenario: Projected sea-level rise and storm surge.
claims.limitations: Projected risk, not a reported failure.

claims.locator: PDF p. 44 (printed p. 45), Ngardok Nature Reserve and water-supply assessment.
claims.paraphrase: Ngardok Nature Reserve covers one-third of Melekeok and supplies its only drinking water; prolonged drought is identified as its greatest natural-system threat, alongside flood and erosion risks.
claims.limitations: Risks are not quantified as service or household impacts.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 44–45 (printed pp. 45–46), Melekeok assessment outputs and implementation status.
claims.paraphrase: Proposed outputs included resilient wastewater, watershed and water-supply systems plus a state adaptation plan; no project adaptation strategies had yet been implemented.
claims.limitations: 2013 recommendations and status; later implementation was not checked.

claims.paraphrase: The Ngerikiil watershed in Airai supplies about four million gallons daily to Airai and Koror and serves roughly 75% of Palau’s population.
claims.limitations: Policy-reported system capacity and population share; no state-specific outage rate is supplied.

claims.locator: PDF p. 20, section 6.1.1, outlying-island supply paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: The policy says households on remote atolls including Kayangel, Sonsorol and Hatohobei mostly rely on rainwater catchments rather than piped treated water.
claims.limitations: The policy does not give atoll-specific household counts or catchment reliability data.

claims.locator: PDF p. 20, Koror–Airai and rural Babeldaob water-treatment descriptions.
claims.paraphrase: While Koror–Airai water quality is described as good, small rural Babeldaob plants often have high turbidity after heavy rain and sometimes detect E. coli or coliforms.
claims.limitations: Policy describes common service conditions but provides no measured prevalence by village.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 11 and 22, drought/water-resource and utility-finance sections.
claims.paraphrase: The policy records that the 2016 drought brought water shortages, poor sanitation, crop failures and malnutrition risk; it also says utility financial shortfalls prevent needed quality improvements in smaller systems.
claims.limitations: Drought conditions are from 2016; the policy does not quantify current household-level effects.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2, executive summary; pp. 22–23, Iporu/Tobi site assessment and recommendations.
claims.paraphrase: At Iporu on Tobi, surveyors found erosion had exposed archaeological remains; low-lying Tobi cultural sites (3–4 metres and below) were considered at risk of inundation.
claims.scenario: Projected inundation risk; no sea-level scenario is specified.
affected_groups: Palauan communities with cultural ties to Tobi
institutions: Bureau of Cultural and Historical Preservation
claims.limitations: Selected heritage sites, not a representative household study.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 24–27, Kayangel traditional-village assessment and recommendations.
claims.paraphrase: The report describes 2012–13 typhoon-driven debris, saltwater inundation affecting Kayangel gardens and homes, and flooding again in April 2021 at the low-lying traditional-village sites.
institutions: Bureau of Cultural and Historical Preservation
claims.limitations: The source documents site and event conditions; it does not attribute individual storms to climate change.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 33–34, Odalmelech monolith assessment in Melekeok State.
claims.paraphrase: At the Melekeok coast, four stone monoliths had been undercut by erosion and were resting on the beach; the report recommends restoring and reinforcing the site and keeping a drainage culvert clear.
institutions: Bureau of Cultural and Historical Preservation
claims.limitations: Observed conditions are from the survey; proposed restoration is not reported as completed.

claims.locator: UNESCO page, paragraphs describing strategy design and community dependence on the reef.
claims.paraphrase: The Rock Islands Southern Lagoon resilience strategy was co-designed over two years by the local management authority and community with NGO and scientific partners, drawing on reef-condition data and community dependence on reef resources.
institutions: Rock Islands Southern Lagoon management authority
claims.limitations: UNESCO programme account; it does not quantify how many households depend on the reef.

claims.locator: UNESCO page, strategy implementation and financing paragraphs.
claims.paraphrase: The strategy account says earlier plans lacked implementation funds and integration; its first phase includes cultural-site preservation, sustainable fisheries, conservation finance and adaptive-management capacity, with a resilience officer placed in Koror State Government.
claims.limitations: Strategy outputs and staffing are reported; no outcome evaluation is presented.

claims.locator: UNESCO page, paragraph on coastal fisheries management plan adopted in 2021.
claims.paraphrase: The local authority adopted a 2021 coastal-fisheries plan applying traditional knowledge to reef-fish and invertebrate recovery and sustainable harvesting for the Koror community.
institutions: Rock Islands Southern Lagoon management authority
claims.limitations: The plan is reported as adopted; the publisher page gives no measured ecological or livelihood outcomes.

claims.locator: Official climate-office page, Palau Climate Change Policy section.
claims.paraphrase: The Office of Climate Change says the PCCP 2025 covers nine sectors and five pillars and is accompanied by a ten-year action plan developed through a two-year process involving 150-plus people.
claims.limitations: Official page summarizes policy architecture; the action plan's delivery is not evaluated there.

claims.locator: Official climate-office page, ‘Key Climate Impacts in Palau’ sections on reefs, storms and sea level.
claims.paraphrase: The Office page projects annual widespread coral bleaching by 2040 and stronger typhoon intensity; it says rising sea level will worsen high-tide flooding, storm surge and erosion.
claims.scenario: The official webpage gives these projections but does not identify an emissions scenario.
claims.limitations: Projection methods are not on the page; the 2040 statement should not be treated as observed bleaching frequency.

claims.locator: UNDP page, paragraph reporting Typhoon Haiyan damage in 2013.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports Typhoon Haiyan caused severe multi-sector infrastructure damage in Palau in 2013, with an estimated 454 homes destroyed or damaged.
claims.limitations: National historical estimate; the report does not attribute this typhoon to climate change.

claims.locator: UNDP page, paragraphs on the 2016 El Niño drought and remoteness-related response planning.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP says the 2016 El Niño drought caused water shortages across 80% of Palau and sanitation risks; NEMO noted the country’s remoteness delays resources and that assessment training can improve response planning.
claims.limitations: The drought statistic and NEMO statement are historical; the source does not disaggregate the 80% by island.

claims.locator: UNDP page, training and partnership paragraphs.
claims.paraphrase: A February 2020 UNDP–SPC–NEMO partnership planned five-day post-disaster assessment and recovery training for 30 officials and stakeholders, 40% women, across sectors including gender, water, health and housing.
claims.limitations: Training was scheduled, not confirmed completed; planned participant counts are not measured capacity outcomes.

access_audit.locator: Complete 98-page government communication, especially printed pp. 41–45; direct PDF text inspected.
access_audit.notes: Read the full publisher-hosted PDF sections supporting each cited claim; historical assessment vintage is flagged.
Directly read the publisher-hosted PDF passages on watershed supply, atoll water access, rural system quality and drought; climate projections are identified as sourced from the 2015 policy.

access_audit.locator: Complete 53-page Phase I assessment, including Iporu/Tobi pp. 22–23, Kayangel pp. 24–27 and Melekeok pp. 33–34.
access_audit.notes: Directly read complete report. Cover credits the Palau cultural-preservation office and University of Oregon researchers; field visits were in 2019–20, with a 2021 Kayangel event noted.
access_audit.reuse_terms: SPREP catalog lists a public licence for the Palau State of Environment dataset, but that does not establish reuse terms for this report; no explicit report licence confirmed.

access_audit.locator: Complete UNESCO publisher page, paragraphs on strategy design, funding, first-phase actions, Koror staffing and 2021 fisheries plan.
access_audit.notes: Directly read the page body; claims retain the reported strategy and implementation scope.

access_audit.locator: Official climate-office body, Palau Climate Change Policy and Key Climate Impacts sections.
access_audit.notes: Directly read the official page's substantive summary; underlying policy and projection methodology were not downloaded or reviewed.

access_audit.locator: Complete UNDP publisher article, paragraphs on 2013/2016 impacts, remote logistics and planned training.
access_audit.notes: Directly read full publisher body; training is described as scheduled in February 2020, not verified as completed.

search_audit.query: Palau official local climate exposure and differentiated vulnerability: state, outer-atoll, water, coastal, cultural heritage and livelihood evidence
search_audit.outcome: Read government climate/water assessments and a targeted ten-site cultural-heritage field survey; named examples include Melekeok, Airai/Koror, Kayangel and Tobi. National aggregates and old assessment dates are retained as limitations.

search_audit.query: Palau climate or disaster impacts explicitly mediated through conflict, violence, displacement, protection, social cohesion or resource tensions
search_audit.outcome: Searches did not identify a directly inspected Palau-specific source establishing a climate-to-conflict or climate-to-violence pathway; none is asserted. Climate-related service, livelihood and cultural impacts are not relabeled FCV outcomes.

search_audit.query: Palau conflict, insecurity, gender-based violence, land or access constraints affecting climate adaptation and disaster recovery
search_audit.outcome: No directly inspected country-specific evidence showed conflict or insecurity constraining adaptation. The sources do document institutional, finance and remoteness constraints; these are kept as capacity limits, not conflict mechanisms.

search_audit.query: Palau community resilience capacity: local watershed, water security, reef/fisheries management and disaster preparedness
search_audit.outcome: Read the water policy, Rock Islands strategy, official climate-policy summary and UNDP preparedness account. Distinguish policy actions and planned training from measured results.

gaps: No directly inspected source established a Palau-specific climate-to-violent-conflict, violence or insecurity pathway; searches are not evidence that such pathways are absent.
The national communication's detailed Melekeok vulnerability assessment dates to 2013; it should be treated as a site-specific historical assessment, not a current condition check.

The SPREP-hosted cultural-site assessment covers ten selected sites rather than representative community or household vulnerability; its site/event findings do not attribute individual storms to climate change.
The 2025 water policy carries forward some projections from the 2015 climate policy; the separate OCC web page does not provide projection methods or scenarios.
The UNDP 2020 article reports a national drought-affected share and planned training without island-level outage disaggregation or confirmation of training completion.
